classification.difficultyReason: Factorise six quadratics, sketch their parabolas and select the correct sign regions, including endpoints and a downward-opening parabola.

content.prompt: Factorise the LHS, then sketch an appropriate parabola in order to solve:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+2x-3&=(x+3)(x-1)\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens upwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-3$ and $1$. It is below the axis between these zeroes, so $-3<x<1$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with zeroes −3 and 1 and y-intercept −3; no grid is supplied or required.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-5x+4&=(x-1)(x-4)\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens upwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $1$ and $4$. It is on or above the axis outside these zeroes, so $x\le1$ or $x\ge4$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with zeroes 1 and 4 and y-intercept 4.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+6x+8&=(x+4)(x+2)\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens upwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-4$ and $-2$. It is above the axis outside these zeroes, so $x<-4$ or $x>-2$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with zeroes −4 and −2 and y-intercept 8.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-x-6&=(x+2)(x-3)\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens upwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-2$ and $3$. It is on or below the axis between these zeroes, so $-2\le x\le3$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with zeroes −2 and 3 and y-intercept −6.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x^2-x-3&=(x+1)(2x-3)\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens upwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-1$ and $\frac32$. It is on or below the axis between these zeroes. Include both zeroes because the inequality is non-strict: $-1\le x\le\frac32$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with zeroes −1 and 3/2 and y-intercept −3.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4+3x-x^2&=(x+1)(4-x)\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens downwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-1$ and $4$. It is above the axis between these zeroes, so $-1<x<4$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with zeroes −1 and 4 and y-intercept 4.
